subject: B
topic: All topics of GK & Current Affairs India (mixed)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar when General Dyer ordered firing on a peaceful gathering. Option 1918 predates it, while 1920 marks the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement and 1921 its spread; none of these coincides with the massacre, so 1919 is the only correct year.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian National Congress:

(i) It was founded in 1885.
(ii) A.O. Hume played a key role in its formation.
(iii) Its first session was held in Bombay.
(iv) Its first president was Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Congress was founded in 1885 with A.O. Hume's initiative, and its first session met in Bombay, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the first president was W.C. Bonnerjee, not Tilak. Hence every option containing (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is popularly known as the 'Nightingale of India'?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu earned the sobriquet 'Nightingale of India' for her lyrical poetry and was also a freedom fighter. Lata Mangeshkar was a singer but is not given this title, Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was a diplomat, and Kamala Das was a poet without this epithet, so only Sarojini Naidu fits.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following leaders with their popular names:

Column I:
(a) Mahatma Gandhi
(b) Subhas Chandra Bose
(c) Lal Bahadur Shastri
(d) Bhagat Singh

Column II:
(i) Netaji
(ii) Shaheed-e-Azam
(iii) Father of the Nation
(iv) Man of Peace

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Gandhi is the Father of the Nation, Bose is Netaji, Shastri is remembered as the Man of Peace, and Bhagat Singh is Shaheed-e-Azam, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii). The other options wrongly swap Netaji with Gandhi or attach Shaheed-e-Azam to Shastri, which do not match historical usage.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The currency of Japan is the:
questions.explanation: Japan's official currency is the Yen. The Won is the currency of South Korea, the Yuan (Renminbi) belongs to China, and the Ringgit is used in Malaysia, so all three are currencies of other Asian nations and only the Yen is correct for Japan.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are landlocked countries?

(i) Nepal
(ii) Bhutan
(iii) Bangladesh
(iv) Sri Lanka

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Nepal and Bhutan are entirely surrounded by land and have no sea coast, so they are landlocked. Bangladesh borders the Bay of Bengal and Sri Lanka is an island nation, so both have coastlines. Hence only (i) and (ii) qualify; any option including Bangladesh or Sri Lanka is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: How many permanent members does the United Nations Security Council have?
questions.explanation: The Security Council has five permanent members (China, France, Russia, the UK and the USA) with veto power. The figure 15 is the total membership including ten non-permanent members, 10 is the number of non-permanent members alone, and 7 has no basis, so only 5 is correct for permanent members.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is a permanent member of the UN Security Council.
Reason (R): The UN Security Council has five permanent members with veto power.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: The reason is factual: there are five veto-wielding permanent members. However India is not among them, so the assertion is false. Thus (A) is wrong while (R) is correct. The first two options fail because (A) is false, and the third fails because (R) is a true statement about the Council.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Constitution of India came into force on __________.
questions.explanation: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day. 15 August 1947 is Independence Day, 26 November 1949 is the date it was adopted (Constitution Day) but not yet enforced, and 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti, so only 26 January 1950 marks its commencement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the wheat production (in lakh tonnes) of a state:

2020 — 30
2021 — 35
2022 — 45
2023 — 40

In which year was the production the highest?
questions.explanation: Comparing the four figures, 45 lakh tonnes in 2022 is the highest, ahead of 40 in 2023, 35 in 2021 and 30 in 2020. 2023 is the second highest, not the peak, while 2020 and 2021 are clearly lower, so 2022 recorded the maximum production.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the longest river in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga, at about 2,525 km within India, is the country's longest river. The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India but shorter than the Ganga, the Brahmaputra's greater length lies mostly outside India, and the Yamuna is a tributary of the Ganga, so the Ganga is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution:

(i) The Right to Equality is a Fundamental Right.
(ii) The Right to Property is a Fundamental Right.
(iii) The Right to Constitutional Remedies is a Fundamental Right.
(iv) The Right against Exploitation is a Fundamental Right.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Rights to Equality, to Constitutional Remedies, and against Exploitation are all Fundamental Rights, so (i), (iii) and (iv) are true. Statement (ii) is false because the Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment (1978) and is now only a legal right, so any option containing (ii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which gas is the most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere, by far the most abundant gas. Oxygen is second at roughly 21%, argon is under 1%, and carbon dioxide is only about 0.04%, so none of these approaches nitrogen's share, making nitrogen the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following trophies with their sports:

Column I:
(a) Ranji Trophy
(b) Durand Cup
(c) Ryder Cup
(d) Thomas Cup

Column II:
(i) Football
(ii) Golf
(iii) Cricket
(iv) Badminton

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy is for cricket, the Durand Cup for football, the Ryder Cup for golf and the Thomas Cup for badminton, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv). The other options swap football with golf or badminton with golf, which contradicts the well-known sport associated with each trophy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nobel Prize is NOT awarded in which of the following fields?
questions.explanation: Nobel Prizes are awarded in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economic Sciences, but not in Mathematics. Physics, Literature and Peace are all recognised Nobel categories, so they are wrong choices; mathematics is honoured instead by awards like the Fields Medal, making it the correct exception.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Union Territories of India?

(i) Ladakh
(ii) Puducherry
(iii) Goa
(iv) Chandigarh

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Ladakh, Puducherry and Chandigarh are Union Territories, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Goa became a full-fledged state in 1987, so (iii) is wrong. Any option that includes Goa as a Union Territory is therefore incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi became India's first (and so far only) woman Prime Minister in 1966. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of an Indian state, Pratibha Patil was the first woman President, and Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister, so none of them held the office of Prime Minister first.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Tropic of Cancer passes through India.
Reason (R): India lies partly in the Northern Hemisphere.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the Tropic of Cancer does pass through India, and India lies in the Northern Hemisphere. However, merely being in the Northern Hemisphere does not by itself explain why this specific latitude crosses the country, so (R) is not the correct explanation. The other options fail because both statements are in fact true.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The book 'Wings of Fire' is an autobiography of:
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, co-written with Arun Tiwari. Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India', Gandhi wrote 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth', and Vikram Sarabhai did not author this book, so only Kalam is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about SAARC:

(i) It was established in 1985.
(ii) Its headquarters is in Kathmandu.
(iii) It has eight member countries.
(iv) India is not a member.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: SAARC was established in 1985, is headquartered in Kathmandu, and has eight members, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because India is a founding member of SAARC. Every option that includes (iv) is therefore incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, as chairman of the Drafting Committee, is regarded as the chief architect of the Constitution. Rajendra Prasad was President of the Constituent Assembly, Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution, and Patel chaired other committees, but none led the drafting, so Ambedkar is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Parliament:

(i) It consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
(ii) The Rajya Sabha is the lower house.
(iii) Money bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
(iv) The Lok Sabha is directly elected by the people.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Parliament comprises the President and two houses, money bills originate only in the Lok Sabha, and the Lok Sabha is directly elected, so (i), (iii) and (iv) are true. Statement (ii) is false because the Rajya Sabha is the upper house, not the lower house, so any option including (ii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Charminar is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Charminar, built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, stands in Hyderabad. Delhi is famous for the Red Fort and Qutub Minar, Agra for the Taj Mahal, and Bijapur for the Gol Gumbaz, so none of these cities hosts the Charminar, making Hyderabad correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following national parks with their states:

Column I:
(a) Kaziranga
(b) Gir
(c) Jim Corbett
(d) Sundarbans

Column II:
(i) Uttarakhand
(ii) Gujarat
(iii) West Bengal
(iv) Assam

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Kaziranga is in Assam, Gir in Gujarat, Jim Corbett in Uttarakhand and the Sundarbans in West Bengal, giving (a)-(iv), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii). The other options swap Assam with Gujarat or Uttarakhand with West Bengal, which misplaces these well-known parks.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule currently lists 22 scheduled languages after successive amendments. The figure 18 reflects an earlier count before later additions, while 24 and 15 do not match any stage of the Schedule, so 22 is the correct present-day number.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are recognised classical languages of India?

(i) Tamil
(ii) Sanskrit
(iii) Hindi
(iv) Telugu

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Tamil, Sanskrit and Telugu are among the languages officially granted classical status, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Hindi, though widely spoken and an official language, has not been given classical language status, so any option that includes Hindi is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The currency of the United Kingdom is the:
questions.explanation: The UK uses the Pound Sterling as its currency. The Euro is used by many EU members but not the UK, the Dollar is used by the USA and others, and the Franc was formerly used by France and Switzerland, so the Pound Sterling is the correct answer for the United Kingdom.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mount Everest is located in India.
Reason (R): The Himalayas form the northern boundary of India.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: The reason is true: the Himalayas form India's northern boundary. But Mount Everest lies on the Nepal–China (Tibet) border, not in India, so the assertion is false. Hence (A) is wrong while (R) is right; the first two options fail because (A) is false, and the third fails because (R) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The first Governor-General of independent India was __________.
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten served as the first Governor-General of independent India from 1947. C. Rajagopalachari was the last (and first Indian) Governor-General, Lord Wavell was Viceroy before independence, and Rajendra Prasad became the first President, so only Mountbatten fits the role first.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the number of medals won by a country in four Asian Games:

2010 — 65
2014 — 57
2018 — 70
2022 — 107

In which year did the country win the most medals?
questions.explanation: The 2022 tally of 107 medals is the highest of the four editions, ahead of 70 in 2018, 65 in 2010 and 57 in 2014. 2018 is the second best, not the maximum, while 2010 and 2014 are clearly lower, so 2022 saw the most medals.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The idea of the Preamble of the Indian Constitution was inspired by the Constitution of:
questions.explanation: The concept of a Preamble was borrowed from the Constitution of the United States. From the UK India took parliamentary government, from Ireland the Directive Principles, and from Canada a strong federal centre, so those are wrong; the Preamble specifically follows the American model.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Directive Principles of State Policy:

(i) They are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution.
(ii) They are justiciable in a court of law.
(iii) They aim to establish a welfare state.
(iv) They were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles are in Part IV, aim at a welfare state, and were inspired by the Irish Constitution, so (i), (iii) and (iv) are true. Statement (ii) is false because the Directive Principles are non-justiciable and cannot be enforced by courts, so any option including (ii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in the year:
questions.explanation: Gandhi began the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 to protest the salt tax, launching the Civil Disobedience Movement. 1928 was the year of the Bardoli Satyagraha, 1932 saw the Poona Pact, and 1942 marks the Quit India Movement, so 1930 is the correct year for the Salt March.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following authors with their books:

Column I:
(a) R.K. Narayan
(b) Arundhati Roy
(c) Vikram Seth
(d) Chetan Bhagat

Column II:
(i) The God of Small Things
(ii) Malgudi Days
(iii) Five Point Someone
(iv) A Suitable Boy

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: R.K. Narayan wrote 'Malgudi Days', Arundhati Roy 'The God of Small Things', Vikram Seth 'A Suitable Boy' and Chetan Bhagat 'Five Point Someone', giving (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii). The other options swap Roy's and Narayan's works or interchange Seth and Bhagat, which are factually wrong pairings.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'bully' is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: A 'bully' is a method historically used to restart play in field hockey. Cricket uses terms like 'over' and 'googly', tennis uses 'deuce' and 'ace', and football uses 'offside', so none of these matches 'bully', which belongs specifically to hockey.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following rivers flow westward into the Arabian Sea?

(i) Narmada
(ii) Tapti
(iii) Godavari
(iv) Krishna

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapti are west-flowing rivers that empty into the Arabian Sea. The Godavari and Krishna flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal, so they do not belong here. Hence only (i) and (ii) are correct, and any option including the Godavari or Krishna is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana' is primarily related to:
questions.explanation: The Jan Dhan Yojana aims at financial inclusion by opening bank accounts for all households. Rural housing is covered by PM Awas Yojana, crop insurance by PM Fasal Bima Yojana, and skill development by PMKVY, so those schemes address different goals and financial inclusion is the correct focus.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Kolkata is a major jute-producing centre.
Reason (R): India is one of the largest producers of jute in the world.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the Kolkata region is a major centre of the jute industry, and India is among the world's largest jute producers. However, India's overall production ranking does not by itself explain why Kolkata in particular is a hub (which owes to the Hooghly and local climate), so (R) does not correctly explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The chemical symbol for gold is:
questions.explanation: Gold's symbol Au comes from its Latin name 'aurum'. Ag is the symbol for silver (from 'argentum'), Gd stands for gadolinium, and 'Go' is not a valid element symbol, so only Au correctly represents gold on the periodic table.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Reserve Bank of India:

(i) It was established in 1935.
(ii) It is the central bank of India.
(iii) It issues the one-rupee note.
(iv) It regulates the monetary policy of the country.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The RBI was established in 1935, is India's central bank, and regulates monetary policy, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are true. Statement (iii) is false because the one-rupee note is issued by the Ministry of Finance (signed by the Finance Secretary), not the RBI, so any option with (iii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The First War of Indian Independence (the Revolt) occurred in the year:
questions.explanation: The great revolt against British rule, often called the First War of Independence, broke out in 1857. 1847 predates it, 1867 comes a decade later, and 1885 is the year the Indian National Congress was founded, so 1857 is the only correct year for the uprising.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's physical divisions:

(i) The Northern Plains are formed largely by alluvial deposits.
(ii) The Deccan Plateau lies to the south of the Northern Plains.
(iii) The Thar Desert is located in eastern India.
(iv) The Western Ghats run roughly parallel to the western coast.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Northern Plains are alluvial, the Deccan Plateau lies to their south, and the Western Ghats parallel the west coast, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are true. Statement (iii) is false because the Thar Desert is in western India (mainly Rajasthan), not the east, so any option including (iii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong was the first human to set foot on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission in 1969. Buzz Aldrin followed him as the second, Michael Collins remained in the command module, and Yuri Gagarin was the first human in space but never landed on the Moon, so Armstrong is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following countries with their currencies:

Column I:
(a) USA
(b) Russia
(c) China
(d) Bangladesh

Column II:
(i) Rouble
(ii) Taka
(iii) Dollar
(iv) Yuan

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The USA uses the Dollar, Russia the Rouble, China the Yuan and Bangladesh the Taka, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii). The other options swap the Rouble with the Yuan or misplace the Taka, which do not match each country's official currency.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Wular Lake, one of the largest freshwater lakes in India, is located in:
questions.explanation: Wular Lake, fed by the Jhelum, lies in the Kashmir Valley of Jammu & Kashmir. Rajasthan has salt lakes like Sambhar, Kerala has the Vembanad backwaters, and Odisha has the brackish Chilika Lake, so none of them hosts Wular, making Jammu & Kashmir correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are principal organs of the United Nations?

(i) General Assembly
(ii) Security Council
(iii) World Trade Organization
(iv) International Court of Justice

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The General Assembly, the Security Council and the International Court of Justice are principal organs of the UN, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. The World Trade Organization is a separate international body and not a UN organ, so any option that includes it is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: A form of government in which power is exercised by the people through elected representatives is called a:
questions.explanation: A representative democracy vests power in the people, who elect representatives to govern. A monarchy is rule by a king or queen, an oligarchy is rule by a small group, and an aristocracy is rule by a privileged class, none of which centres on popular election, so democracy is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha can be dissolved like the Lok Sabha.
Reason (R): The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house whose members retire in rotation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: The reason is true: the Rajya Sabha is a permanent house with one-third of members retiring every two years. Because it is permanent, it cannot be dissolved, so the assertion is false. Hence (A) is wrong while (R) is correct; the first two options fail because (A) is false, and the third fails because (R) is true.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the highest civilian award of India.
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award. The Padma Vibhushan and Padma Shri rank below it among the Padma awards, and the Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime military decoration, not a civilian award, so only the Bharat Ratna correctly completes the sentence.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the foreign tourist arrivals (in lakhs) in India:

2015 — 80
2016 — 88
2017 — 100
2018 — 106

In which year was the increase over the previous year the largest?
questions.explanation: The year-on-year increases are +8 in 2016, +12 in 2017 and +6 in 2018, so 2017 had the largest rise. 2016's gain of 8 and 2018's gain of 6 are both smaller, and 2015 is the base year with no prior figure, so 2017 is the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Ayushman Bharat' scheme is associated with:
questions.explanation: Ayushman Bharat provides health insurance cover for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation to poor families. Education schemes such as Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, housing schemes like PM Awas Yojana, and farm schemes like PM-KISAN address other sectors, so health insurance is the correct association.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian monsoon:

(i) The southwest monsoon brings most of India's annual rainfall.
(ii) It generally arrives in Kerala in June.
(iii) The southwest monsoon reaches northwest India before it reaches Kerala.
(iv) The northeast monsoon brings winter rain to Tamil Nadu.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon gives most of the annual rain, arrives in Kerala around June, and the northeast monsoon brings winter rain to Tamil Nadu, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are true. Statement (iii) is false because the monsoon reaches Kerala first and advances to the northwest later, so any option with (iii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, the first Indian and Asian laureate. C.V. Raman won in Physics in 1930, Mother Teresa won the Peace Prize in 1979, and Amartya Sen won in Economics in 1998, so all of them came after Tagore, who was first.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following famous places with their cities:

Column I:
(a) Gateway of India
(b) Hawa Mahal
(c) Golden Temple
(d) Meenakshi Temple

Column II:
(i) Amritsar
(ii) Mumbai
(iii) Madurai
(iv) Jaipur

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Gateway of India is in Mumbai, Hawa Mahal in Jaipur, the Golden Temple in Amritsar and the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai, giving (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii). The other options swap Mumbai with Jaipur or Amritsar with Madurai, which misplaces these landmarks.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Wimbledon tennis championship is held in:
questions.explanation: Wimbledon, the oldest Grand Slam, is played in London on grass courts. Paris hosts the French Open (Roland Garros), New York the US Open, and Melbourne the Australian Open, so those are different Grand Slam venues and London is correct for Wimbledon.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Fundamental Duties under the Indian Constitution?

(i) To respect the National Flag and the National Anthem
(ii) To protect and improve the natural environment
(iii) To pay income tax on time
(iv) To safeguard public property

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Respecting national symbols, protecting the environment and safeguarding public property are all Fundamental Duties under Article 51A, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Paying income tax, while a legal obligation, is not listed among the Fundamental Duties, so any option including (iii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which vitamin is produced in the human body on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Sunlight (ultraviolet rays) helps the skin synthesise Vitamin D, essential for calcium absorption. Vitamin C comes from citrus fruits, Vitamin A from carrots and leafy greens, and Vitamin K is linked to blood clotting and gut bacteria, so none of these is made by sunlight, making Vitamin D correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cherrapunji receives very heavy rainfall.
Reason (R): India's monsoon winds are seasonal in nature.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: Cherrapunji is among the wettest places on Earth, and the monsoon winds are seasonal. However, the mere seasonality of the monsoon does not explain Cherrapunji's extreme rainfall, which is caused by the orographic lifting of moist winds over the Khasi Hills, so (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The international organization that regulates trade among nations is the:
questions.explanation: The World Trade Organization (WTO) frames and enforces the rules of international trade. The IMF handles global monetary stability, the World Bank funds development projects, and UNESCO works on education, science and culture, so none of them regulates trade, making the WTO the correct body.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about ASEAN:

(i) It was formed in 1967.
(ii) Its headquarters is in Jakarta, Indonesia.
(iii) India is a founding member of ASEAN.
(iv) It is a regional grouping of Southeast Asian nations.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ASEAN was formed in 1967, is headquartered in Jakarta, and is a grouping of Southeast Asian nations, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are true. Statement (iii) is false because India is not a member of ASEAN (only a dialogue partner), so any option that includes (iii) is wrong.
